summary: The v5.7.1 apparent body-width implementation is traceable, calibrated, rotation-tested, explicitly separated from legacy EDT width, and handles insufficient geometry with NaN. However, the production-wide claim fails measurement-geometry review because the reported 3D tortuosity does not trace a reconstructed 3D path: it combines a projection-plus-Z numerator with a denominator assembled from a potentially different within-plane endpoint distance and the track Z span. The required synthetic and adversarial known-geometry validation for 3D length, tortuosity, volume, gaps, and orientation is also absent. These deficiencies block acceptance of the high-risk production claim.

findings.title: Reported 3D tortuosity is not the tortuosity of a reconstructed 3D path
findings.impact: The field can be presented and aggregated as curvature of a reconstructed nucleus even though neither its numerator nor denominator follows a common 3D centerline. This violates the requirement that the numerical quantity represent its stated geometry and blocks the high-risk production claim.
evidence: sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:5259-5274 separately aggregates maximum per-plane geodesic length, maximum per-plane endpoint distance, and first/last centroids.

sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:5295-5309 defines the numerator as sqrt(maximum lateral length squared plus Z span squared), but defines the denominator as sqrt(maximum per-plane endpoint distance squared plus Z span squared); these components need not describe the same plane or endpoints.

sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:12681-12688 and sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:12809-12813 describe the field as estimated 3D path length divided by 3D end-to-end distance and interpret it as curvature.
The same construction is duplicated in sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:5464-5507 for the global-assignment summary path.
findings.recommendation: Either reconstruct and measure an explicit calibrated 3D centerline with a denominator using the same endpoints, or rename the current quantity as a projection-plus-Z proxy and remove claims that it measures 3D path tortuosity or curvature. Preserve the existing field as an explicitly named legacy/proxy field.

findings.title: No known-geometry validation for the production 3D measurements
findings.impact: Formula, anisotropy, orientation, gap, endpoint, clipping, and volume errors can pass the current tests. The claim's acceptance criterion requiring automated and adversarial measurement validation is therefore unmet.
evidence: tests/test_saturn_v571_body_width.py:58-150 validates only the 2D body-width path and its missing-value behavior.

Tests identified by repository search use supplied track-summary values for reporting assertions but do not derive expected 3D quantities from controlled masks or coordinates; examples include tests/test_saturn_v57_multisample.py:517-518 and tests/test_saturn_v57_multisample.py:896-902.
V5_7_1_VALIDATION_REPORT.md:92-97 reports a prior full-suite pass but does not identify a synthetic 3D geometry test or its expected values.
findings.recommendation: Add focused synthetic tests for horizontal, vertical, oblique, curved, single-slice, anisotropically sampled, boundary-truncated, and gapped tracks. Assert calibrated Z span versus coverage, projection-plus-Z length, true or explicitly proxied tortuosity, filled-mask volume, and all clipping/missing-value behavior.

findings.title: Gapped-track volume semantics are implicit
findings.impact: For a track spanning missing planes, volume_um3 sums observed planes only while z_covered_um spans every index between endpoints. Users may interpret volume as a continuous reconstruction even though missing slabs are neither interpolated nor flagged in the measurement name.
evidence: sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:5226-5229 permits gaps according to TRACK_MAX_GAP_SLICES.
sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:5286-5290 defines coverage from the complete first-to-last index range.
sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:5302-5303 sums only observed area rows multiplied by one Z step.
sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:12687-12688 describes volume as the sum of filled-mask pixels across slices, without stating the gapped-track policy.
findings.recommendation: Label the field as observed-slice mask volume or explicitly record missing-slice count and interpolation policy. Add a gapped-track synthetic test and ensure reports disclose whether missing slabs are omitted or estimated.

findings.title: Body width is an apparent 2D mask measurement, not biological chromatin width
findings.impact: Even a technically correct contour-chord value cannot establish PSF-corrected physical chromatin width, ultrastructure, compaction, or a biological group effect.
evidence: sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:3258-3328 measures chords of a segmented 2D mask.
sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:12788-12792 explicitly lists PSF, focus, resolution, and mask-boundary dependence.
V5_7_1_VALIDATION_REPORT.md:67-73 calls the quantity apparent body-mask width and declines group inference.
findings.recommendation: Retain the apparent-mask qualifier in every table, figure, and biological interpretation.

limitations: No full image stack was run, as prohibited by the review instructions.
Focused pytest execution was unavailable because pytest is not installed in the active Python 3.14 environment; static inspection and test-source review were used instead.

The working tree is pre-commit and contains modifications/untracked audit infrastructure, although git rev-parse confirmed HEAD d8c498ca3c76b17ce76c02dc85bed5d9ac542d0b. This review did not inspect other reviewers' outputs.
Visual agreement of generated pilot PDFs with source tables was not independently verified in this measurement-geometry review.
recommended_follow_up: Supersede this audit run after correcting or renaming the 3D tortuosity field and adding known-geometry tests.
Install the repository's declared test environment and rerun the focused body-width, dual-head, calibration, 3D aggregation, and new adversarial geometry tests.
Document observed-slice volume behavior for gapped tracks and expose missing-slice provenance in track and report tables.
Keep body_width_um as apparent mask width and retain width_um_dt_median_legacy as an explicitly legacy definition.
